source.work: Firebase Admin SDK documentation, client versus server setup
source.paraphrase: The Admin SDK runs with full service-account privilege and belongs in server code only, never in shipped client bundles.

invariants.why: firebase-admin in client code ships service-account privilege to the browser. That is a full project breach, not a scoped leak.
invariants.fixHint: Use firebase/auth on the client. Keep firebase-admin behind server files outside app, components, pages and their src mirrors.
invariants.avoid: require() loads the same SDK as import. Renaming the import does not change the module specifier.

source.paraphrase: currentUser is null when nobody is signed in. Read it into a variable and handle null before touching its fields.

invariants.why: Chaining off currentUser throws the moment a signed-out user reaches the code, usually on the exact screen that should invite sign-in.
invariants.fixHint: Assign currentUser first and return early on null, or subscribe with onAuthStateChanged and render from the callback value.
invariants.avoid: getAuth().currentUser is still nullable. Optional chaining passes this rule but still needs a fallback for the signed-out case.

source.work: Firebase Cloud Functions documentation, HTTP triggers and CORS
source.paraphrase: Browser-callable cross-origin handlers need appropriate CORS handling; same-origin and server-to-server handlers may not.

invariants.why: The syntax cannot tell whether the caller is a browser on another origin or whether a wrapper sets CORS headers.
invariants.fixHint: Wrap the body with cors(req, res, () => ...) in the same onRequest statement so the middleware cannot be dropped.
invariants.avoid: An async handler still answers without CORS headers. A bare named function reference carries no middleware with it.

source.paraphrase: listAll pages through everything under a ref. Page with list() and maxResults instead.

invariants.why: listAll on a growing prefix gets slower and pricier with every upload. One prefix with user content can stall the caller.
invariants.fixHint: Call list(ref, { maxResults: n }) and follow page tokens. Choose n from what the UI renders.
invariants.avoid: A narrow user-scoped prefix is still unbounded. Counting items still downloads every item first.

source.work: Firebase documentation, Upgrade from the namespaced API to the modular API
source.paraphrase: The firebase/compat libraries keep the namespaced API working during migration. They are a temporary solution that will be removed completely in a future major SDK version, and they do not get the size benefits of the modular API.

invariants.why: Compat code breaks when a future major SDK removes the compat libraries, and it ships the whole namespaced SDK instead of only the functions the app imports.
invariants.fixHint: Import functions from the modular entry points (firebase/app, firebase/auth, firebase/firestore, ...) and call them with the instance, for example getDoc(doc(db, "orders", id)).
invariants.avoid: A side-effect import such as import "firebase/compat/firestore" still loads compat, even when the visible calls are modular. Remove it rather than keep it next to modular code.

source.work: Firebase documentation, Add Firebase to your JavaScript project (firebase.google.com)
source.paraphrase: initializeApp creates the default Firebase app instance; calling it more than once without checking existing apps via getApps() throws a duplicate app error.

invariants.why: When initializeApp() lives inside a helper or request handler without a getApps().length check, the second invocation crashes with FirebaseError: Firebase App named '[DEFAULT]' already exists.
invariants.fixHint: Initialize Firebase once at module scope, or guard with getApps().length ? getApp() : initializeApp(config).
invariants.avoid: Module-top-level initializeApp(config) calls are allowed. Guards placed in a caller function outside the helper are not visible.
